solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: A great deal, reduced green fruit

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, so the last letter of the phrase's synonym is dropped

parts.note: a great deal means many, as in a great many
green means go, the green traffic light that lets you proceed

explanation.surface: A shopper is offered a discount on unripe tropical fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green fruit' reads as unripe fruit, but 'green' gives GO and only 'fruit' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The mango is a tropical stone fruit, so it is an example of a fruit.

clue.text: Venturesome sort reaches top of this?

definitions.text: Venturesome sort reaches top of this?

parts.words: Venturesome sort reaches top of this?
parts.note: the clue asks what summit an adventurous climber aims for, the world's highest peak

explanation.surface: An adventurer climbs to the summit of something.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the mountain whose summit is the ultimate prize for bold climbers.
explanation.definitionFit: The Himalayan peak is the highest on Earth, the goal of daring mountaineers.

clue.text: Female admitted to finest academy

indicators.note: admitted to means let in, so the name sits within the two words

explanation.surface: A woman wins a place at the best academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Nesta is a woman's given name, so it stands for a female.

clue.text: Absolute decision by two umpires in agreement?

definitions.meaning: complete, thoroughgoing, as in a total rogue

definitions.text: decision by two umpires in agreement?
definitions.meaning: in cricket both umpires giving the batsman out, a verdict given twice over

explanation.surface: Two umpires agree on a final ruling.
explanation.definitionFit: Out-and-out means utter or complete, and two umpires each saying out give the phrase literally.

clue.text: Headache as fighter plane almost came down

parts.note: a MiG is a Soviet or Russian fighter jet

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the final letter of the verb is lost

parts.note: rain that came down is said to have rained

explanation.surface: Someone gets a headache from a fighter jet that nearly crashed.
explanation.definitionFit: A migraine is a severe recurring kind of headache, often with nausea.

clue.text: Essential to store up appellation controlee wine

indicators.note: to store means to keep inside, so the essential holds the abbreviation

parts.note: a must is something essential

indicators.note: up means read upwards in a down clue, so the letters are reversed

parts.note: AC is the abbreviation for appellation controlee, the French wine quality label

explanation.surface: A wine with official French status is a must to keep in the cellar.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscat is a sweet wine made from muscat grapes, so a kind of wine.

clue.text: Guardsman trained to ignore posh old ladies?

indicators.note: trained means drilled into new shape, so the letters are rearranged
to ignore means leaving a letter out of the mix

parts.note: U is the label for upper-class or posh usage

explanation.surface: A trained guardsman pays no attention to well-to-do elderly women.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove U from GUARDSMAN and rearrange the rest. The question mark warns that 'old ladies' is a loose definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandmothers are typically elderly women, hence old ladies with a question mark.

clue.text: Room At The Top script — it was returned, with odd bits excised

indicators.note: returned means sent back, so the kept letters are read in reverse
with odd bits excised means the first, third, fifth letters and so on are cut out, keeping the even ones

explanation.surface: The script of the novel Room at the Top was sent back with odd passages cut.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of 'script it was' are C, I, T, T, A, which reversed give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An attic is the room at the very top of a house, under the roof.

clue.text: Upwardly-mobile ladies manage to employ one?

definitions.text: Upwardly-mobile ladies manage to employ one?

indicators.note: upwardly-mobile means moving upwards in a down clue, so the letters are read in reverse
to employ means to take on, so the pieces hold the numeral inside

parts.note: dames are ladies
I is one as a Roman numeral
to manage is to run

explanation.surface: Socially ambitious women can manage to hire a child's servant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Upwardly-mobile' looks like a description of social climbers, but in a down clue it signals reading the assembled letters from the bottom up.
explanation.definitionFit: A nursemaid is a servant hired by well-off families to look after the children.

clue.text: Mediocre university student initially works about half the weekend

indicators.note: about means going round, so the first piece wraps around the day

parts.note: the weekend is Saturday and Sunday, so half of it is Saturday, short SAT

indicators.note: initially means only the opening letter of the word student is used

parts.note: works means a factory, as in a steelworks

explanation.surface: A mediocre undergraduate works for part of the weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' sits after 'works' but acts on the plural of 'university' plus the student's initial, which goes round the half-weekend; 'works' stays a plain synonym at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsatisfactory work falls short of an acceptable level, which is what mediocre suggests.

clue.text: Fish in batter's served after cold offal dish

indicators.note: served after means placed behind, so the piece comes after the letter for cold

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

indicators.note: in means placed within the batter's word

parts.note: a batter is a hitter, and the 's makes it hitter's
a ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: Fish in batter is served after a cold plate of offal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' suggests frying, but it is a cricketer or baseball hitter.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitterlings are pig's intestines, cooked as a dish of offal.

clue.text: Old soldiers not allowed, it's announced, on public transport

indicators.note: on means placed after, the convention in an across clue

parts.note: a train is a form of public transport

indicators.note: announced means spoken out, so the word for not allowed is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: not allowed means banned

explanation.surface: Veteran soldiers find they are barred from public transport.
explanation.walkthrough: A trainband was a citizen militia company in London from the 16th to 18th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: Trainbands were companies of trained citizen militia of earlier centuries, hence old soldiers.

clue.text: Oral examination in foreign language

indicators.note: oral means spoken, so the word for examination is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: an examination is a check

explanation.surface: A student faces a spoken test in a foreign language.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oral examination' looks like a single phrase, but 'Oral' signals the sound and 'examination' gives the word heard.
explanation.definitionFit: Czech is the language spoken in the Czech Republic, so it is a foreign language to an English speaker.

clue.text: Recordings of six sample tapes lacking musicianship, principally

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is removed

parts.note: demos are sample recordings sent out by bands

indicators.note: principally means first of all, so only the opening letter of musicianship counts

explanation.surface: A band's six demo tapes show no musical talent.
explanation.definitionFit: Videos are recordings of pictures and sound on tape or disc.

clue.text: Daily Express leaders having various details of least interest

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the two newspaper words
various means of different kinds, so the letters of details are rearranged

explanation.surface: The Daily Express front pages carry assorted dull details.
explanation.walkthrough: The Daily Express is a British national tabloid newspaper; 'leaders' suggests its editorials.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadliest here means dullest, the most boring, so of the least interest.

clue.text: Graduate in his own time getting important post on board

parts.note: MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate
his own refers back to the graduate, so it is MA'S

explanation.surface: A graduate working at his own pace lands a key job on a company board.
explanation.walkthrough: 'post on board' suggests a boardroom job; the board is a ship's deck.
explanation.definitionFit: The mainmast is the principal pole on a sailing ship, so a chief post aboard.

clue.text: Scotsman turned up before meal carrying power tool

indicators.note: before means placed ahead of the next piece
turned up means flipped upwards in a down clue, so the name reads backwards

parts.note: Ian is a typical Scottish man's name

indicators.note: carrying means holding inside, so the meal wraps the letter

parts.note: lunch is a meal
P is the abbreviation for power in physics

explanation.surface: A Scotsman shows up before lunch with a power tool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'power tool' reads as one thing, but 'power' gives P and only 'tool' defines.
explanation.definitionFit: A nail punch is a small hand tool for driving nail heads below the surface.

clue.text: Severely criticise a climber

parts.note: to monster someone is British slang for criticising them harshly

explanation.surface: Someone harshly criticises a mountaineer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climber' suggests a mountaineer; it is a climbing plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Monstera, the Swiss cheese plant, is a tropical climbing vine.

clue.text: Editor's job, concealing Democrat opposition to political change

indicators.note: concealing means hiding away, so a letter is taken out of sight

parts.note: redaction is the editing of a text for publication

explanation.surface: An editor's work hides a Democrat's opposition to reform.
explanation.definitionFit: Reaction in politics is resistance to progress or reform, the stance of reactionaries.

clue.text: Awkward task for doctor

definitions.meaning: a fiddly job needing finicky handling
to doctor accounts is to falsify them

explanation.surface: A doctor faces a tricky job.
explanation.definitionFit: A fiddle is a fiddly, awkward job, and to fiddle figures is to doctor or falsify them.

clue.text: English team in a row, losing at home, is sent abroad

parts.note: XI is eleven in Roman numerals, a cricket or football team

indicators.note: losing means giving up, so letters are taken out

parts.note: things in a row are lined up
in means at home

explanation.surface: An English team lined up, beaten at home, is sent overseas.
explanation.definitionFit: To be exiled is to be banished from one's country, so sent away abroad.

clue.text: Cream envelope containing meal ticket

indicators.note: containing means holding inside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: SAE is a stamped addressed envelope
LV is a luncheon voucher, a British meal ticket given by employers

explanation.surface: An envelope holds a voucher for a meal along with some cream.
explanation.definitionFit: A salve is a soothing ointment, so a kind of cream for the skin.

clue.text: Small delicate female stuck in swirling river

indicators.note: stuck in means placed inside, so the letter goes within the river
swirling means turning round, so the river's name is reversed

parts.note: the Nile is the great African river

explanation.surface: A small delicate woman is caught in a swirling river.
explanation.definitionFit: Elfin describes someone small and delicate, like an elf.

clue.text: IT guarantee covers old type of software

indicators.note: covers means wraps around, so the guarantee goes outside

parts.note: a seal is a mark of guarantee, as in a seal of approval
ex means former, so old
an app is an application program

explanation.surface: An information technology warranty covers outdated software.
explanation.walkthrough: IT is not information technology but 'it', the old slang for allure.
explanation.definitionFit: It, as in the It girl, is old slang for personal allure and attractiveness.

clue.text: Competitors go after points

indicators.note: after means placed behind the compass letters

parts.note: E and N are compass points, east and north
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: Competitors chase points.
explanation.definitionFit: The entry for a contest is the whole body of competitors taking part.

clue.text: Have a good moan, during first bits of German tutorial, about course

parts.note: to beef is to complain or moan
well means good, as in all is well
during means in

indicators.note: first bits means the opening letter of each of the two words

parts.note: on means about, as in a talk on a subject

explanation.surface: A student complains loudly in a German tutorial about the syllabus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'course' looks like a course of study; it is a course of a meal.
explanation.definitionFit: Beef Wellington is fillet steak baked in pastry, served as a main course at dinner.

clue.text: Level of attainment rose, perhaps

definitions.meaning: the grade or benchmark that work must reach
a rose grafted onto a tall upright stem, trained as a small tree

explanation.surface: A rose bush sets a benchmark.
explanation.definitionFit: A standard is a required level, and a standard rose is one grown on a single tall stem.

clue.text: Former US president creating confusion in speech

indicators.note: in speech means as spoken, so the word is heard not spelt

parts.note: a haze is a state of mental confusion

explanation.surface: A former president's speeches cause confusion.
explanation.walkthrough: Rutherford B. Hayes was the 19th US president, 1877 to 1881.
explanation.definitionFit: Rutherford B. Hayes served as President of the United States in the 1870s.
